status: DRAFT expected-answer key for human grading; review it before you start and do not change it after you have seen an answer

authoring.author: the AI assistant (the same author as the questions, the gold labels and overlay v1.1): the key is therefore NOT an independent validation
derived_only_from: preregistration (question, evidence phrases, gold ids; sha256 cb7a05a1...)
the pre-retrieval audit results/nist_prereg_review_sheet.md ('Expected answer (from the source only)' lines, written before any retrieval)
authoring.answer_text_seen_before_writing: The assistant had seen the text of the answers for E1, O1, A4, E3, N5 and O6 (displayed in earlier reports) before writing this key. No answer text was used to define any expected answer, required point or unsupported-claim example; those six entries were written from the passages and the audit lines in the same way as the other eighteen.
authoring.verification: every quoted supporting passage is asserted to be an exact substring of its frozen chunk (here and in tests/check_frozen_artifacts.py)

correctness.reference: the expected answer in this key (derived from the frozen source), independent of which passages the model was shown
correctness.correct: all required points are present, the required polarity and any required qualification/exception/negation are conveyed, nothing contradicts the source
correctness.partially_correct: the main direction is right but a required qualification/exception/component is missing, or an included detail is wrong or unsupported
correctness.incorrect: the answer contradicts the source, answers a different question, or gives no answer (including the refusal sentence when the expected answer exists in the corpus)

evidence_support.reference: the passages shown to THAT answer (listed in the sheet), not the whole NIST publication
evidence_support.fully_supported: every substantive claim is stated in, or directly entailed by, the shown passages
evidence_support.partially_supported: some substantive claim is not in the shown passages
evidence_support.unsupported: the main claim is not in the shown passages (a claim can be true in the full PDF and still be unsupported by the shown passages)

completeness.reference: the required points of this key; complete = every point marked required (and the qualification where qualification_affects is 'completeness') is present

unsupported_claims.rule: 'present' = at least one substantive claim that is neither stated in nor directly entailed by the shown passages (see unsupported_claim_examples per query); describe it in the notes field. A citation to the wrong passage does not by itself make a claim unsupported: judge the claim against the shown passages.

overall_judgment.suggestion: acceptable = correct, fully supported, no unsupported claims; unacceptable = incorrect or unsupported; borderline = everything else. Add a one-sentence justification.

paired_judgment.rule: judged on the combination of correctness, evidence support and completeness, not on length or style; objective citation checks must not decide it

conventions: Refusal convention: the exact refusal sentence makes no factual claim, so unsupported_claims = none and evidence_support = fully supported; correctness = incorrect (the expected answer is missing) and completeness = incomplete. Apply the same convention to every refusal.

Grade against this key, not against the other answer. Do not use the objective citation checks (cites a gold chunk, only supplied passages, refusal sentence, sentence count) as evidence of correctness.
Retrieval success (lenient/strict outcome, ranks), the objective format checks and your human grades are three separate metrics; never merge them.
If you disagree with an item of this key, do not edit it while grading: record the disagreement in reviewer_notes and decide afterwards whether to issue a dated key v1.1.

The one-line 'Your grading (blank)' prompt under each query is the ORIGINAL free-text prompt and is kept unchanged. In the CSV use the vocabulary of this legend (for `better`: 'A1 better' / 'A2 better' / 'neither clearly better').
O2 and O3 carry scope decisions from overlay v1.1 (see their grader_notes).

queries.expected_answer: Likelihood of initiation/occurrence = the chance a threat event is started (adversarial) or occurs (non-adversarial). Likelihood of impact = the chance that, once initiated or occurring, it results in adverse impact, regardless of the magnitude of harm. The overall likelihood combines the two.
required_points: States that one likelihood is that the event is initiated/occurs.
States that the other is that, once initiated, it results in adverse impact (not the size of the harm).
(Completeness) mentions that the overall likelihood combines the two.
queries.qualification: The likelihood of impact is about whether harm results, 'regardless of the magnitude of harm' (it is not the severity).
queries.acceptable_wording: Any faithful paraphrase; 'probability' and 'chance' are interchangeable.
unsupported_claim_examples: Describing the likelihood of impact as the severity or size of the harm.
Swapping the two definitions.
Stating that the two are multiplied or combined by a specific formula (the guide specifies no algorithm; see also N1).

supporting_passages.quote: The likelihood of impact addresses the probability (or possibility) that the threat event will result in an adverse impact, regardless of the magnitude of harm that can be expected.
